original_question: For which cardinals κ does the Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property, meaning that every Riemann integrable function f: [0, 1] → ℓ_2(κ) is weakly continuous almost everywhere?
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Problem 3.2: "For which cardinals κ does the space ℓ_2(κ) have the WLP?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost exactly: it asks about the same family of spaces, ℓ_2(κ); it asks for the same classification by cardinals κ; and it correctly expands WLP as the requirement that every Riemann integrable map f:[0,1]→ℓ_2(κ) be weakly continuous almost everywhere.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces, so ℓ_2(κ) is the real Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ), not the complex one.
[0,1] is understood with its Lebesgue measure.
“Weakly continuous” means continuous with respect to the weak topology on ℓ_2(κ).
“Almost everywhere” means outside a Lebesgue null subset of [0,1].
The intended notion of Riemann integrability is the usual norm-valued Riemann integrability for Banach-space-valued functions.
The survey frames this as an open problem in its own right, not as the broader neighboring problem of characterizing all Banach spaces with the weak Lebesgue property.
No restriction to uncountable κ is stated; the problem ranges over arbitrary cardinals.
refined_question: For which cardinals κ does the real Hilbert space ℓ_2(κ) have the weak Lebesgue property; that is, for which κ is it true that every norm-Riemann integrable function f:[0,1]→ℓ_2(κ), where [0,1] is equipped with Lebesgue measure, is continuous almost everywhere with respect to the weak topology of ℓ_2(κ)?
justification: In arXiv:1607.07787, your draft corresponds directly to the survey's exact open problem in Section 3.1, Problem 3.2. The sentence immediately before Problem 3.2 defines the weak Lebesgue property (WLP), and the notation section fixes the ambient conventions that the paper deals with real Banach spaces and Lebesgue measure on [0,1]. So the paper-faithful refinement is not to broaden the question, but only to make those implicit conventions explicit while staying with the exact Problem 3.2 formulation. The nearby Problem 3.1 is broader, asking to characterize Banach spaces having the LP, so your draft should stay with the narrower WLP/ℓ_2(κ) problem instead.
